input: He denies current chest pain and has not experienced a definite blackout, although he occasionally feels light-headed when getting out of the cab.
At today's examination, uncorrected visual acuity measures 6/12 in the right eye and 6/18 in the left eye, with each eye tested separately before glasses were applied.

The optometrist's signed sheet confirms the measurements; the driver believes a newer pair of glasses improves road-sign reading, but no corrected measurement has yet been entered, and the nurse does not substitute that impression for a measured corrected acuity.
Current visual measurements and the documented blackout are available, while the event mechanism, recurrence history and specialist advice remain incomplete.
The driver experienced a witnessed blackout during a break four weeks earlier.
The driver recalls being hot and hungry before the event, yet neither vasovagal syncope nor hypoglycaemia has been confirmed, and cardiac monitoring is still pending.
He says there may have been an earlier episode of light-headedness without loss of awareness, which the nurse has not counted as a second blackout.
His father used hearing aids, which does not establish the driver's threshold.
